featured.title: The $100,000 Toll Most Employers Paid Anyway: What Mullin’s Numbers Reveal About the H-1B
featured.excerpt: DHS told the Senate that more than 200,000 of fiscal 2026’s 286,000 H-1B applicants paid the six-figure fee for faster processing — a sign the program isn’t dying, but is being rationed by wealth.
featured.image_caption: Stacks of US one-hundred-dollar bills — the H-1B premium fee now totals $100,000 per petition
featured.nri_angle: Indians receive close to three-quarters of all H-1B visas, so the revelation that 70% of applicants paid the $100,000 fee — and that it lands hardest on rural hospitals hiring Indian-trained doctors and on smaller employers — reshapes who from India can realistically reach America.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian Founder Now Runs the App 500 Million Indians Use Every Day
news.excerpt: Meta has handed WhatsApp to CRED's Kunal Shah and poured $900 million into his fintech startup. The bet is that a man who built a consumer app in India can finally crack what WhatsApp has never managed there: payments at scale.
news.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED, who has been named global head of WhatsApp
news.nri_angle: WhatsApp is the connective tissue of diaspora family and business life from the Gulf to North America, and an Indian-built fintech founder now runs it globally — a marker of Indian operators, not just Indian users, reaching the top of the world's biggest platforms.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Fourteen Students Walked Into a Coaching Centre in Lucknow. They Never Walked Out.
news.excerpt: A fire tore through a crowded building in Lucknow's Aliganj on Monday, killing 14 — most of them young people — as some jumped from windows to escape. The cause is still unknown. The pattern, in India's tightly packed coaching towns, is not.
news.image_caption: Fire and emergency services in India; a coaching-centre fire in Lucknow's Aliganj killed 14 on June 22
news.nri_angle: India's coaching-centre ecosystem is the same machine that, years downstream, produces the students and professionals the diaspora is built from; the recurring fire-safety failures that killed 14 in Lucknow are a tax on exactly the middle-class ambition NRIs celebrate, and a marker of the gap between India's pitch to returning talent and its enforcement on the ground.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Rewrote the Rulebook for Foreigners Who Want to Stay. The Diaspora's Spouses and Kids Are the Quiet Winners.
news.excerpt: In a wave of changes flowing from its new immigration law, India has stretched employment and business visa extensions to ten years, folded a tangle of visa types into cleaner categories, added e-visa options and slashed the salary bar for interns. For OCI families and foreign-passport relatives, the paperwork of belonging just got lighter.
news.image_caption: India has stretched employment and business visa extensions to ten years as part of a wide overhaul of its visa system
news.nri_angle: From foreign-passport spouses and children of OCI cardholders to returning professionals and diaspora-founded startups hiring abroad, the people whose lives span two countries are the first to feel India's quieter immigration reforms — longer stays and lighter paperwork, set against a more tightly tracked system.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Has Flown 1,700 of Its Own Out of a War Zone. The Planes Are Still Going Back for More.
news.excerpt: Under Operation Sindhu, special flights from Mashhad, Yerevan and Ashgabat have brought home more than 1,700 Indians from Iran, with hundreds more from Israel routed through Jordan. For families of students and workers caught in the Iran-Israel war, each landing is a name crossed off a list.
news.image_caption: Special flights under Operation Sindhu have brought more than 1,700 Indian nationals home from Iran through Delhi airport
news.nri_angle: An estimated 32 million Indians live abroad, many in the volatile arc from the Gulf to the Levant; Operation Sindhu reaffirms the unwritten contract behind every Indian passport — that when a war zone closes in on students, workers and pilgrims overseas, New Delhi will send the planes to bring them home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Rupee's Best Run in Months Just Ended. The Reason Sits in Washington, Not Delhi.
news.excerpt: India's currency snapped a six-day winning streak on Monday to close near 94.68 a dollar, as a hawkish US Federal Reserve lifted the greenback to a one-year high. For the diaspora sending money home, a weaker rupee is a quiet windfall.
news.image_caption: Indian rupee notes alongside US dollars; the rupee snapped a six-session winning streak on Monday to close near 94.68 a dollar
news.nri_angle: India is the world's largest recipient of remittances — a record ~$137-140 billion expected this fiscal year — so every move in the rupee directly changes how far a diaspora dollar stretches when it lands in family accounts, school fees and investments back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Nearly 18,000 Indians Are Trapped at Sea in the Gulf. Three Have Already Come Home in Coffins.
news.excerpt: Indian crews man the tankers caught between a US blockade and Iran's threats around the Strait of Hormuz. As food and water run short on stranded ships, New Delhi has lodged its strongest protest yet with Washington.
news.image_caption: A crude oil tanker underway; Indian crews man many of the vessels caught in the standoff around the Strait of Hormuz
news.nri_angle: Indian seafarers crew a large share of the world's commercial fleet and send wages home to families across Kerala, Goa and Andhra Pradesh; with nearly 18,000 stranded in the Gulf and four already dead, the standoff is a stark reminder that the diaspora abroad includes the mariners whose safety can hinge on a conflict they have no part in.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Starmer Just Quit. The Man Likely to Replace Him Has Said Nothing About the India Trade Deal That Starts in Three Weeks.
news.excerpt: Keir Starmer resigned as British prime minister on Monday, clearing the way for Andy Burnham to become Britain's seventh leader in a decade. The India-UK free trade pact is set to take effect on July 15 — and the diaspora is about to find out whether a change at the top changes anything.
news.image_caption: Andy Burnham, the Greater Manchester mayor widely expected to become Britain's next prime minister
news.nri_angle: Britain is home to about 1.9 million people of Indian origin, and the India-UK trade deal due to take effect July 15 touches the price of goods, the cost of UK postings, and the value of money moved between two of the diaspora's home countries — all now in play during a prime-ministerial handover and a sliding pound.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Boston Judge Killed the $100,000 H-1B Fee. The Government Wants It Back Before You Can Exhale.
news.excerpt: Judge Leo Sorokin ruled the fee an illegal tax Congress never authorised, handing a reprieve to the Indian workers and doctors who make up the bulk of H-1B holders. But the decision is paused, three courts are now split, and the fight is heading to appeal.
news.image_caption: The federal courthouse in Boston, where Judge Leo Sorokin struck down the $100,000 H-1B fee
news.nri_angle: Roughly three in four H-1B visas go to Indian workers, and Indians are the largest group of international students feeding the program — so a court fight over the $100,000 fee directly decides whether the American pathway thousands of diaspora families planned around stays open or stays priced out.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Oil Is Falling After the Iran Deal. Your Flight to India Is Not Going to Get Cheaper Anytime Soon.
news.excerpt: Airlines are about to save tens of billions on fuel as crude slides on the back of the US-Iran ceasefire. But tight capacity means carriers plan to pocket the relief, not pass it on — and the diaspora's long-haul routes are squarely in the squeeze.
news.image_caption: An airport departures board; airlines plan to bank fuel savings rather than cut fares (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: NRIs fly some of the most fuel-intensive long-haul routes in the world, many transiting the Gulf hubs analysts say are least likely to see fare cuts — so the oil windfall from the Iran deal will pad airline margins rather than lower the price of the family flight home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Gathered the Security Chiefs of China, Russia and Iran in One Delhi Room. Doval Is in the Chair.
news.excerpt: The BRICS National Security Advisers' Meeting opens in New Delhi on Monday, with Wang Yi and Sergei Shoigu among the delegates. The agenda is cyber, AI and terrorism — but the subtext is India's bid to steer a bloc that now stretches from Beijing to Brasilia.
news.image_caption: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, who chairs the BRICS NSA Meeting in New Delhi
news.nri_angle: BRICS is an argument over whose rules govern global trade, technology, currency and security — the same forces behind the tariffs, visa rules and rupee swings that buffet NRIs abroad, and the safety of the India their families still call home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Explosion Tore Through Qatar's Biggest Gas Hub. The Search Is On for 18 Missing in a City Built by Indian Hands.
news.excerpt: A blast and fire at the Barzan plant in Ras Laffan left 54 injured and 18 missing on Sunday night. In a country where Indians are the single largest community, the diaspora is now waiting on the casualty list.
news.image_caption: A gas flare and power lines in Qatar's Ras Laffan industrial area, the hub of the country's gas industry
news.nri_angle: Indians are the single largest community in Qatar — roughly 730,000 to 830,000 people, about a fifth of the population, with a heavy presence in the oil, gas and construction sectors where Sunday's deadly blast occurred, leaving hundreds of thousands of families waiting on the casualty list.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Monsoon Was Supposed to Break the Heat. Three Weeks In, the Rain Gauges Are Still Running a Third Empty.
news.excerpt: Cumulative rainfall is running nearly 38% below normal, Mumbai is rationing water, and farmers are delaying planting. For a diaspora that watches India's food prices and the rupee, a weak start to the monsoon is a number worth tracking.
news.image_caption: Monsoon clouds gather over bare, unsown farmland in India as a weak start delays kharif planting
news.nri_angle: A weak monsoon drives up India's food inflation — the biggest component of headline inflation — which shapes interest rates and the rupee, the currency that values every NRI remittance and deposit, and hits families back home through costlier vegetables, water shortages and rural incomes tied to the harvest.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Made Cough Syrup a Prescription Drug. The Backstory Is the Deaths of More Than 140 Children.
news.excerpt: A quiet amendment to a 1945 rulebook strips the word 'syrup' from the list of medicines that can be sold over the counter. Behind it lies a contamination scandal that battered India's standing as the 'pharmacy of the world'.
news.image_caption: India has removed cough syrups from the over-the-counter exemption list, requiring sale through licensed pharmacies
news.nri_angle: India's role as the 'pharmacy of the world' is a point of national pride and a lifeline for patients globally; with many NRIs relying on familiar Indian-made medicines, the contamination deaths abroad and the scandal-driven tightening of rules at home speak directly to whether 'made in India' medicine can be trusted.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Pakistan's Defence Minister Says It Will 'Go to War' With India Over Water. The Treaty Has Been Suspended Since Last Year.
news.excerpt: Khawaja Asif's latest threat lands as Pakistan battles a severe internal water crisis affecting nearly a third of its population — and as New Delhi keeps the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty firmly in abeyance, more than a year after the Pahalgam attack.
news.image_caption: Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who threatened war with India over the suspended Indus Waters Treaty
news.nri_angle: Water has now joined Kashmir and trade as a structural flashpoint between two nuclear-armed neighbours, and even hollow-sounding war threats raise the baseline of risk for diaspora families with roots on both sides of the border — a genuine escalation would ripple through remittances, travel, energy prices and the safety of relatives back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Third Community Has Been Drawn Into Manipur's War. Now the Kukis Are Begging Modi to Step In.
news.excerpt: What began in 2023 as a Kuki-Meitei conflict has spread to the Nagas. With 14 Kuki civilians reported killed, 11 villages burnt and roads to the hills blockaded, Manipur's apex Kuki body has handed a memorandum to the Prime Minister warning of abandonment.
news.image_caption: Manipur, where escalating Kuki-Naga violence has left 14 reported dead and 11 villages burnt
news.nri_angle: Many in Manipur's Kuki and Naga communities are Christian, and their plight has drawn faith-based and human-rights networks abroad; diaspora groups with northeastern roots have pressed for greater central intervention and humanitarian access, frustrated that a conflict of this scale has not commanded the national or global attention it warrants.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Trade Minister Just Summoned Washington's Negotiator to Delhi. The Clock Runs Out July 24.
news.excerpt: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer arrives this week to put 'final touches' on the first phase of a bilateral trade deal — one both sides want signed before a temporary tariff regime expires and a new, harsher one could snap into place.
news.image_caption: India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, who is hosting US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in Delhi this week
news.nri_angle: The tariff line these two ministers settle on directly sets the shelf price of Indian goods in America and the health of the pharma, textile, gems and IT export industries that employ millions of the diaspora's relatives back home — making a deal before the July 24 cliff a pocketbook issue for NRIs, not just a diplomatic one.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Ambani Just Filed the Papers for What Could Be India's Biggest-Ever IPO. The Diaspora's Phone Carrier Is Going Public.
news.excerpt: The board of Jio Platforms approved its draft prospectus on June 19 and filed with India's market regulator the same day, clearing the way for a Mumbai listing that bankers say could raise around $3.8 billion — and that Mukesh Ambani called Reliance's 'most important value-creation milestone this year.'
news.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, who announced the Jio Platforms IPO filing at the company's annual general meeting
news.nri_angle: Jio is the carrier that connects nearly half a billion Indians — the network NRIs use to call home, stream cricket and run UPI payments — so its record IPO is both a chance for overseas Indians to invest in the backbone of their own ties to India and a marquee test of whether Indian tech can list at global scale.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: One Warning From Accenture Knocked India's IT Stocks to a Three-Year Low. The Diaspora's Bellwether Sector Is Flashing Red.
news.excerpt: When the world's largest consulting firm flagged cautious client spending and a $400 million Middle East hit, India's tech index tumbled to levels last seen in 2023 — dragging Infosys, TCS and Wipro and shaking the industry that employs and exports the most diaspora talent.
news.image_caption: An Indian IT services campus; the sector's stocks fell to a three-year low after Accenture's cautious outlook
news.nri_angle: India's IT majors are the largest formal channel sending Indian tech talent to the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf, so when the sector's stocks hit a three-year low on warnings of frozen client budgets, it signals slower hiring, fewer onsite postings and tighter visa sponsorship — the levers that directly shape diaspora careers.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Immigrant Now Runs One of Manhattan's Most Closely Watched Neighborhoods. A 250-Year-Old Award Just Made the Point.
nri-world.excerpt: Raju Mann, the India-born head of New York's Battery Park City Authority, was honored at Federal Hall among five naturalized citizens recognized for shaping Lower Manhattan — a quiet marker of how far Indian-origin leadership has moved into the machinery of American cities.
nri-world.image_caption: Federal Hall National Memorial in Lower Manhattan, where the Alexander Hamilton Immigrant Achievement Awards are presented
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin success in America has been told largely through the private economy — founders and CEOs. Raju Mann leading a major New York public authority, and being honored among naturalized citizens at Federal Hall, marks the diaspora's quieter move into civic stewardship: not just thriving in a city, but being trusted to govern part of it.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Most Powerful Old-Boys' Network in Tech Isn't From Stanford. It Just Turned 75 and Threw Itself a Party in California.
nri-world.excerpt: When thousands of IIT alumni gathered in Long Beach to mark 75 years of India's elite engineering schools, the real subject wasn't nostalgia. It was the question of what a diaspora network becomes once it stops needing to prove itself.
nri-world.image_caption: A campus of the Indian Institutes of Technology, which mark 75 years in 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: The IIT alumni network is among the most powerful pieces of diaspora infrastructure the world has built — the pipeline behind a generation of Indian-origin technology leaders in the US. Its 75th-anniversary gathering in California, courted by India's ambassador, captures the diaspora at a hinge: confident, courted by the homeland, and increasingly tilting capital and attention back toward India.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Procedure Can Reverse a Stroke in Minutes. Fewer Than 3% of the World Can Get It — and an Indian Doctor Has Spent a Decade Fixing That.
nri-world.excerpt: Dr. Dileep Yavagal, honored with a Lifetime Achievement Award at this year's American Academy of Neurology meeting, helped make clot removal a global standard. His harder fight is over who actually receives it — and in India, the answer is almost no one.
nri-world.image_caption: An interventional procedure in a catheterization suite; mechanical thrombectomy removes stroke-causing clots through a catheter
nri-world.nri_angle: Yavagal is the diaspora story less often told: not the founder or CEO, but the India-trained physician-scientist who reached the top of American medicine and turned it back toward the country he came from. India's ~1.4% access to a stroke treatment that can reverse disability — versus 32% in the US — is a gap that touches NRI families with aging parents in India directly.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Marry Out, and You Are Out: India's Top Court Weighs a Rule That Empties the Fire Temple of Its Daughters
nri-world.excerpt: A nine-judge bench has called the Parsi practice of excommunicating women who marry outside the faith “discriminatory.” For a community of barely 50,000 in India — and a scattered, shrinking diaspora — the stakes are nothing less than survival.
nri-world.image_caption: A Zoroastrian fire temple; India's Supreme Court is weighing whether barring Parsi women who marry outside the faith from such spaces is discriminatory
nri-world.nri_angle: Parsi/Zoroastrian communities are among the most globally dispersed of Indian-origin groups — Mumbai, London, Toronto, Sydney, Hong Kong, the US — and intensely affected by demographic decline. The Supreme Court's scrutiny of excommunicating women who marry outside the faith speaks directly to diaspora Zoroastrians, who face the same patriarchal membership rules in mixed marriages abroad, and whose North American federations remain split over recognising the children of intermarried members.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora Built Itself Around Its Children. Now It Is Building for Its Parents.
nri-world.excerpt: A new India Home senior centre opening in Hicksville on July 7 is a small ribbon-cutting with a large subtext: the first big wave of Indian immigrants to America is growing old, and the community is scrambling to catch up.
nri-world.image_caption: Elderly Indian women; as the first big wave of Indian immigrants to the US grows old, a new India Home senior centre opens in Hicksville, Long Island on July 7
nri-world.nri_angle: The first big wave of post-1965 Indian immigrants to the US is now entering old age, and culturally specific senior care — familiar food, language, festivals — is becoming one of the diaspora's most urgent and under-met needs. The Hicksville centre, replicating India Home's Queens model on suburban Long Island, signals a shift in diaspora priorities from arrival-and-aspiration institutions (temples, scholarships) toward institutions of permanence, with the same greying wave cresting from the Bay Area to Houston to Toronto and London.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: ‘Unity in Diversity’: Britain's South Asian Month Tries to Hold a Fracturing Family Together
nri-world.excerpt: South Asian Heritage Month returns to the UK on July 1 with a theme that is part celebration and part plea — a bid to keep eight nations, many faiths and a long, painful history under one tent.
nri-world.image_caption: Diyas and rangoli at a South Asian celebration; the UK's South Asian Heritage Month 2026 runs July 1-31 under the theme 'Unity in Diversity'
nri-world.nri_angle: South Asian Heritage Month is the UK's most institutionally successful diaspora commemoration, and its 2026 'Unity in Diversity' theme is studied by Indian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi community organisers in the US, Canada and Australia as a model for winning government and broadcaster recognition. For the Indian diaspora it is a double-edged platform — prominent but shared under a pan-South Asian umbrella, at a moment when some assert a distinct Indian or Hindu identity, making 'unity' as much an internal aspiration as an external celebration.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Connecticut Diaspora Group Turned 20 by Writing Two $25,000 Checks — and Reading the Room on Immigration
nri-world.excerpt: GOPIO-CT marked two decades by honoring a state senator, a biotech founder, a bank CEO, an engineer and a journalist — then donated $50,000 to local charities, in a year when belonging itself was on the agenda.
nri-world.image_caption: Connecticut State Senator Sujata Gadkar-Wilcox, one of five honorees at GOPIO-CT's 20th anniversary gala
nri-world.nri_angle: GOPIO-CT's 20-year evolution — from cultural preservation to public policy, philanthropy and civic engagement, including $50,000 in donations to non-Indian local charities — is a template for how Indian diaspora organizations across the US, UK and Canada mature into institutions, even as community leaders confront rising anti-immigrant rhetoric aimed at Indians.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: They Grew Up American on Paper. At 21, the Paper Runs Out — and Indians Are Most of Them.
nri-world.excerpt: An estimated 250,000 'documented dreamers' face self-deportation when they age out of a parent's work visa. The Indian diaspora, trapped longest in the green-card backlog, is renewing its push for the America's Children Act.
nri-world.image_caption: The US Capitol, where backers of the America's Children Act are pressing Congress to protect 'documented dreamers' from aging out
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian families dominate the US employment-based green-card backlog, so their children make up a disproportionate share of the estimated 250,000 'documented dreamers' who age out of legal status at 21 — making the bipartisan America's Children Act one of the most direct legislative stakes for the Indian American community.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A $40 Box of Mangoes, a WhatsApp Group, and a Culture War the Diaspora Didn't Ask For
nri-world.excerpt: Indian mango season has become an annual ritual of longing and coordination for the diaspora — until a conservative commentator mocked it, and turned a fruit into a flashpoint over who belongs in America.
nri-world.image_caption: Boxes of Indian mangoes; alphonso and kesar varieties drive a seasonal buying ritual across the diaspora
nri-world.nri_angle: The seasonal scramble for Indian mangoes — alphonso, kesar and regional varieties bought through WhatsApp groups at $40 a box — is one of the diaspora's most vivid rituals of homeland connection, and the backlash to a commentator mocking it shows how even food has become entangled with anxieties over Indian immigrants' place in America.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Is Switching Who Handles Passports in the UAE. For Five Days, the Window Closes Entirely.
nri-world.excerpt: The Indian Embassy in Abu Dhabi says passport, visa and attestation services across the Emirates will halt from June 26 to 30 as a new outsourced provider takes over — a quiet handover that touches one of the world's largest diaspora communities.
nri-world.image_caption: An Indian passport; consular services in the UAE pause June 26-30 during a provider handover
nri-world.nri_angle: The UAE is home to roughly 3.5 million Indians — the largest expatriate group in the country — for whom passport renewals, document attestation and visa paperwork are the machinery of daily life abroad, so a planned five-day service blackout just before an unfamiliar new provider takes over is a deadline every Indian in the Emirates needs to plan around.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: On the Same Saturday, Two Sikh Parades Shut Down Streets 1,200 Miles Apart. Neither Was an Accident.
nri-world.excerpt: From a small Oregon city to a British Columbia mountain town, the Nagar Kirtan has become the diaspora's most visible — and most deliberate — act of public belonging.
nri-world.image_caption: Participants in a Sikh Nagar Kirtan procession and festival at San Francisco's Civic Center
nri-world.nri_angle: For Sikh families abroad, the Nagar Kirtan is both an act of faith and a calculated answer to decades of being mistaken for strangers in their own towns — a once-a-year invitation to neighbours who otherwise never step inside a gurdwara.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Buying a Flat in India Has Long Been a Compliance Nightmare for NRIs. Delhi Just Promised to Fix It.
nri-world.excerpt: From October, a PAN-based system is set to replace the tangle of TAN registrations and non-resident withholding rules that turn an ordinary property purchase into a paperwork ordeal.
nri-world.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs own or plan to buy property in India, and the rules differ sharply depending on whether the person across the table is a resident or a fellow non-resident — a distinction most buyers discover only when the transaction is already half-done.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The Rupee Just Had Its Best Week in Months. Now a Resurgent Dollar Will Test Whether It Holds.
markets-finance.excerpt: A drop in oil after the US-Iran peace deal pushed the rupee to 94.32, its strongest weekly run in 11 weeks — but a dollar at a one-year high and a hawkish Federal Reserve are pulling the currency back, while government bonds wait on the pace of foreign money returning.
markets-finance.image_caption: The rupee posted its best week in months as oil prices fell, before a resurgent dollar tested the gains
markets-finance.nri_angle: Every move in the rupee reprices the remittances NRIs send home, the value of their NRE and FCNR deposits, and the returns on their Indian investments — so a week that swung from oil-driven relief to dollar-driven pressure is not abstract macro news for the diaspora but a direct signal on when to send money and what their India holdings are worth.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Ambani's Jio Files for What Could Be India's Biggest IPO Ever — and This Time, No One Is Cashing Out
markets-finance.excerpt: Jio Platforms has filed draft papers with India's markets regulator for a fresh-issue-only listing of up to 27 crore shares, a deal market estimates put near ₹36,000 crore at a valuation of roughly ₹12.5 lakh crore — with the proceeds aimed squarely at paying down debt rather than handing existing investors an exit.
markets-finance.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, whose Jio Platforms has filed draft papers for a record IPO
markets-finance.nri_angle: Jio touches nearly every Indian family with a phone, and its listing is the marquee event NRI investors have waited years for — a chance to own a slice of the diaspora's most-used digital utility, even as the fresh-issue-only structure and a cooled, war-rattled market raise real questions about price and timing.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: For Once, the Worry Is a Rate Hike: India's Central Bank Holds Steady as War-Driven Oil Tests Its Nerve
markets-finance.excerpt: Minutes of the June meeting show the RBI kept its key rate at 5.25 percent and chose to 'wait and watch' as an Iran-war oil spike sent the rupee tumbling and lifted its inflation forecast to 5.1 percent — even as some economists now bet the next move is up, not down, with HSBC penciling in half a point of hikes this year.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India held its key rate at 5.25 percent as a war-driven oil spike clouded the inflation outlook
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs sending money home, parking savings in Indian deposits or holding rupee assets, the prospect of rate hikes rather than cuts flips the usual calculus — it can lift returns on Indian fixed deposits and steady the rupee, but it also signals that war-driven inflation, not growth, is now the force steering India's monetary policy.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreigners Keep Selling Indian Stocks. Indians Keep Buying — and That Has Quietly Rewired the Market
markets-finance.excerpt: In May, foreign investors pulled nearly Rs 33,000 crore out of Indian equities while domestic institutions poured in over Rs 82,000 crore — powered by a record Rs 30,954 crore of monthly SIP contributions across 9.64 crore accounts — a structural shift that means the old reflex of watching foreign flows to call the market is increasingly out of date.
markets-finance.image_caption: Domestic mutual fund inflows have grown large enough to absorb foreign investors' selling of Indian equities
markets-finance.nri_angle: Many NRIs still read foreign-investor outflows as a sell signal for Indian stocks, but a steady tide of domestic SIP money is now large enough to absorb that selling — a shift that should reframe how the diaspora thinks about timing, volatility and where the Indian market's real support now comes from.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Dangling Higher Dollar Rates to Pull NRI Money Home — and Banks Now Want to Route It Through GIFT City
markets-finance.excerpt: After the RBI agreed to absorb the hedging cost on fresh foreign-currency NRI deposits and scrapped the rate caps, banks have pushed dollar deposit rates to 6–7 percent and are seeking permission to fund the inflows through their offshore GIFT City units — part of a drive analysts think could draw $55 billion or more to steady the rupee.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India has sweetened terms on foreign-currency NRI deposits to draw the diaspora's dollars and steady the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: This drive is aimed squarely at the diaspora's wallet: NRIs can suddenly earn 6–7 percent on dollar deposits in Indian banks — nearly double the old rates and with no currency risk — making it one of the most consequential personal-finance shifts for overseas Indians in years.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Courting Foreign Bond Money — but the RBI Wants It Trading at Home, Not Through Euroclear
markets-finance.excerpt: Even after scrapping taxes to lure overseas investors into its government bonds, India's central bank is resisting offshore settlement platforms like Euroclear, insisting foreigners trade directly on the domestic system to keep the market's liquidity in one place.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India wants foreign investors to trade its government bonds on the domestic NDS-OM platform rather than via offshore systems
markets-finance.nri_angle: How freely foreign money flows into India's $1-trillion-plus government bond market shapes the rupee, India's borrowing costs and the stability of the assets NRIs hold back home — so the central bank's careful, on-its-own-terms opening of the market is a quiet signal about the financial backdrop against which the diaspora invests, remits and plans for retirement in India.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Tax Tribunal Says Money NRIs Send Into Their NRE Accounts From Foreign Salaries Cannot Be Taxed as 'Unexplained' Income
markets-finance.excerpt: An income-tax appellate ruling has deleted a tax demand against a non-resident Indian, holding that once funds in an NRE account are shown to come from foreign earnings, the tax department cannot treat them as unexplained money — a quiet but meaningful protection for the diaspora.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's tax tribunal ruled that foreign-salary credits in an NRI's NRE account cannot be taxed as unexplained income
markets-finance.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs route their overseas salaries into NRE accounts in India to support family, buy property or invest — and the fear of a tax notice questioning those inflows is real, so a tribunal confirming that genuinely foreign-earned money parked in an NRE account is not taxable removes a recurring anxiety for the diaspora.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's IT Giants Just Hit a Three-Year Low — and a Warning From Accenture Lit the Fuse
markets-finance.excerpt: Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCLTech tumbled as the Nifty IT index slid to its lowest in three years, after Accenture flagged cautious client spending and a $400 million hit from the Middle East — a chill that runs straight through the diaspora's most familiar industry.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's Nifty IT index fell to a three-year low as Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCLTech slid after a cautious outlook from Accenture
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian IT is the diaspora's home turf — it built the careers, H-1B visas and green cards of a huge share of NRIs in the United States, and its shares are a staple of NRI portfolios — so a slump driven by cautious global tech spending is both a portfolio question and a livelihood question for hundreds of thousands of Indian-origin tech workers abroad.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Biggest Stock Exchange Is Finally Going Public — in What Could Be the Country's Largest IPO Ever
markets-finance.excerpt: After a decade of delays, the National Stock Exchange has filed papers for a roughly Rs 30,000 crore ($3.3 billion) listing — a pure sale of existing shares that could value the bourse near Rs 5 lakh crore and hand its long-locked-in investors a multi-billion-dollar windfall.
markets-finance.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange has filed for what could be India's largest-ever IPO, a roughly Rs 30,000 crore offer for sale
markets-finance.nri_angle: The NSE is the exchange on which most of the Indian shares and funds that NRIs own actually trade, so its own market debut — potentially India's largest ever — is both a marquee investment opportunity for diaspora portfolios and a barometer of how much appetite global money still has for Indian equities after a bruising year of outflows.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Gold Is Supposed to Soar When the World Looks Dangerous. This Year It Is Doing the Opposite.
markets-finance.excerpt: Bullion has logged its sixth straight week of lower or flat closes and is grinding toward $4,000 — far below February's near-$5,600 record — even with a Middle East war and an unsigned ceasefire on the table. The reason is not fear, but a hawkish Federal Reserve and a dollar at a 13-month high.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold has logged six straight weeks of lower or flat closes, sliding toward $4,000 amid a hawkish Fed
markets-finance.nri_angle: Gold is the diaspora's default store of value — in wedding jewellery, in sovereign gold bonds, in the ETFs and coins NRIs buy to hedge a wobbly rupee — so a sharp, counter-intuitive slide in the metal even as geopolitical risk lingers is a direct signal to Indian-origin investors about whether their favourite safe haven is still doing the job they bought it for.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Central Bank Holds Rates and Trims Its Growth Forecast as the West Asia War Clouds the Outlook
markets-finance.excerpt: Minutes from the Reserve Bank of India's June meeting show a rate panel content to wait and watch — holding the repo rate at 5.25 percent while cutting the FY27 growth forecast to 6.6 percent, as the conflict in West Asia muddies the trade-off between inflation and growth.
markets-finance.image_caption: The RBI held its repo rate at 5.25 percent and cut its FY27 growth forecast to 6.6 percent in June
markets-finance.nri_angle: The RBI's growth and inflation calls shape everything NRIs care about back home — the value of the rupee against their salaries abroad, the returns on their Indian deposits and equities, and the cost of money for family and businesses in India — so the central bank's cautious posture and lowered growth forecast are a direct read on the climate for diaspora money.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: After a Record Exodus, Foreign Investors Tiptoed Back Into Indian Stocks This Week
markets-finance.excerpt: Foreign portfolio investors bought a net ₹1,209 crore of Indian equities in the week to June 20 — a small but symbolically important turn after dumping a record $30 billion-plus through 2026, as a US-Iran peace deal and cheaper oil revived appetite for emerging markets.
markets-finance.image_caption: Foreign investors turned net buyers of Indian equities in the week to June 20 after a record 2026 sell-off
markets-finance.nri_angle: Many NRIs hold Indian equities directly or through mutual funds and India-focused ETFs abroad, so a tentative reversal in foreign flows — the single biggest swing factor for Indian stocks this year — matters directly to diaspora portfolios and to anyone weighing whether the worst of 2026's sell-off is behind them.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Sacked the Captain Who Won Them the T20 World Cup — and Left Him Out of the Team Altogether
sports.excerpt: Months after Suryakumar Yadav lifted India's third T20 world title, the selectors have stripped him of the captaincy and his place in the side. Shreyas Iyer, back in the format after two and a half years, inherits the job.
sports.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer, recalled after more than two years, is India's new full-time T20I captain
sports.nri_angle: A World Cup-winning captain dropped months after the trophy lift is a Rorschach test for the diaspora — cold-blooded modernity to some, betrayal to others — and a window on how ruthless India have become about staying atop the white-ball game, the kind of loyalty-versus-results debate that runs hot in NRI WhatsApp groups across time zones.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Picked Its England One-Day Squad, and the Team Sheet Read Like a Changing of the Guard
sports.excerpt: Shubman Gill now captains India in all three formats, Jasprit Bumrah is back, and Yashasvi Jaiswal was left out despite a match-winning hundred. Virat Kohli is in too — if his hamstring lets him be.
sports.image_caption: Shubman Gill, who now captains India across all three formats, will lead the ODI side in England
sports.nri_angle: A squad sheet that captures a generational handover the diaspora has followed with tenderness — the team passing from Kohli and Rohit to Shubman Gill, who now captains across all formats — while the dropping of a centurion (Jaiswal) is exactly the kind of selection debate that lights up NRI WhatsApp groups across time zones, all framed against India's build toward the 2027 ODI World Cup.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Seventeen Years After Her First Match in England, Harmanpreet Kaur Walked Out for Her 200th — a Number No Cricketer Had Ever Reached
sports.excerpt: India's captain became the first player, man or woman, to appear in 200 T20 Internationals. That it happened at a World Cup in the same country where she debuted as a teenager in 2009 made the milestone read like a story written in advance.
sports.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur, India's captain and the first cricketer to play 200 T20 Internationals
sports.nri_angle: Harmanpreet Kaur is one of the players through whom the Indian diaspora embraced the women's game, and her 17-year climb to a record 200 T20Is mirrors the rise of women's cricket in India that NRIs have followed with growing pride — a story of persistence rewarded that resonates across a community built on long journeys far from home.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Most Famous Paddler Missed the Asian Games Team by One Ranking Place
sports.excerpt: Manika Batra, the face of Indian table tennis, has been named only a reserve: world No. 51, one spot short of the top-50 ranking that would have guaranteed her a place. Her public appeal to the Prime Minister has reopened an old fight over how India picks its athletes.
sports.image_caption: Manika Batra receiving the Arjuna Award in 2018
sports.nri_angle: Manika Batra is one of the few Indian Olympic-sport athletes with genuine global recognition, and the row over whether a transparent ranking rule should override proven international pedigree strikes a familiar chord with NRIs who follow India's Olympic-sport rise and value merit-based process.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Europe Just Launched Its First Big-League T20 — and the Diaspora Built Half the Talent Pool
sports.excerpt: The ICC-sanctioned European T20 Premier League opened its player draft this week, with six city franchises across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands — cricketing nations whose teams the South Asian diaspora has quietly powered for years.
sports.image_caption: Malahide Cricket Ground in Dublin, one of Ireland's international venues; the new ETPL will field two Irish franchises, in Dublin and Belfast
sports.nri_angle: The Irish, Scottish and Dutch national teams the ETPL is built to strengthen have for years been substantially powered by South Asian immigrant communities, and a serious, well-broadcast home league gives diaspora families across Britain, Ireland and the Netherlands a top-tier local team to watch and a real professional pathway for their children.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: A Smaller India Heads to Glasgow — and the Sports It Wins Most Aren't on the Bill
sports.excerpt: India will send just 125-130 athletes and staff to a stripped-down Commonwealth Games that has dropped wrestling, badminton, hockey and table tennis — its richest medal seams.
sports.image_caption: Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, one of India's medal hopes in a Glasgow programme that retains weightlifting
sports.nri_angle: The Commonwealth Games have long been the most accessible stage for Indians in Britain, Canada and Australia to watch their country compete, and Glasgow's stripped-down programme — minus India's signature sports of badminton, wrestling and hockey — means fewer of those moments, even as Ahmedabad's 2030 Games promise to bring the event home.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Unbeaten Run Ends at Old Trafford, Undone by a Marizanne Kapp Masterclass
sports.excerpt: Chasing 159, South Africa rode an unbeaten 81 from Marizanne Kapp to beat India by six wickets in Manchester, handing the tournament favourites their first defeat of the Women's T20 World Cup.
sports.image_caption: Marizanne Kapp, whose unbeaten 81 powered South Africa past India at Old Trafford
sports.nri_angle: India's women had built a genuine diaspora following on the back of an unbeaten World Cup start, and this first defeat — in front of a large Indian community in Manchester and over breakfast tables across the US — is the moment that romance met a colder reality, with semifinal seeding now on the line.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Women Won in Auckland, and With It a Ticket Back to the Top Table of World Hockey
sports.excerpt: India beat hosts New Zealand 2-0 to lift the FIH Women's Nations Cup and seal promotion to the Pro League, a year after being relegated from the same elite tier.
sports.image_caption: India goalkeeper Savita, whose side beat New Zealand to win the FIH Women's Nations Cup in Auckland (Wikimedia Commons)
sports.nri_angle: A year after India's women were relegated from world hockey's elite Pro League, an unbeaten Nations Cup run and a final won on New Zealand soil sends them back to the top tier — a redemption arc that resonates with NRI families from London to Toronto to Auckland, where the final was staged in front of a large local Indian community.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Kohli Is Coming Back to England — This Time With a White Ball, and the Diaspora Is Counting Down
sports.excerpt: India recalled Virat Kohli for next month's three ODIs in England, subject to a fitness test. Yashasvi Jaiswal, who replaced him and made a hundred against Afghanistan, was left out.
sports.image_caption: Virat Kohli, recalled to India's ODI squad for the July tour of England, subject to a fitness test
sports.nri_angle: No cricketer moves tickets and travel plans across Britain like Virat Kohli, and his recall means the UK's vast NRI community can watch him at Edgbaston, Cardiff and Lord's in July — a homecoming of sorts staged thousands of miles from home, in the same English summer India began their Test era without him.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Two Hundreds, 460 Runs, One Game: America's Cricket League Just Staged Its Most Brutal Run-Fest Yet
sports.excerpt: Mitchell Owen smashed 155 and Kieron Pollard answered with an unbeaten 100, but Washington Freedom's 245 was 30 too many for MI New York at Grand Prairie.
sports.image_caption: Kieron Pollard, who struck an unbeaten 100 off 56 balls for MI New York at Grand Prairie
sports.nri_angle: MLC was sold to the NRI community as world-class T20 cricket in their own time zone and backyard — and a match where both Mitchell Owen and Kieron Pollard score hundreds, with US international Saurabh Netravalkar in the home XI, is that promise delivered for the diaspora that built American cricket's heartland in suburbs like Grand Prairie.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.excerpt: Japan's emphatic 4-0 victory over Tunisia reshapes Group F dynamics.
sports.image_caption: Estadio BBVA in Monterrey — venue for Tunisia vs Japan at the 2026 FIFA World Cup (Wikimedia Commons)
sports.nri_angle: The Indian-American community, pivotal in North America, added vibrancy and support to the match in Monterrey, illustrating football's unifying power.

technology.title: Two IIT Grads Built a $2 Billion AI Company in Under a Year. They Haven't Shipped a Product Yet.
technology.excerpt: Upscale AI, founded by Palo Alto Networks and Cavium veterans Barun Kar and Rajiv Khemani, just pulled in Nvidia and Azim Premji's fund at a $2 billion valuation — on a thesis about the least glamorous corner of the AI boom.
technology.image_caption: Rows of servers and high-speed networking in a modern AI data center
technology.nri_angle: Two IIT-trained, Bay Area networking veterans built a $2 billion AI infrastructure startup backed by Indian capital (Premji Invest) and Nvidia — a live template for diaspora engineers weighing whether deep-infrastructure expertise still beats chasing the AI-app gold rush.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Qualcomm Spent 20 Years as a Phone-Chip Giant. On Wednesday It Has to Prove It Can Build for the Data Center.
technology.excerpt: At its June 24 Investor Day, CEO Cristiano Amon will unveil the Dragonfly data-center roadmap and possibly a $10 billion acquisition — a pivot that will shape the careers of the thousands of Indian engineers inside Qualcomm.
technology.image_caption: A close-up of a semiconductor wafer, the building block of modern AI chips
technology.nri_angle: Qualcomm's make-or-break data-center pivot will decide whether its large cohort of Indian engineers — in San Diego, the Bay Area, Hyderabad and Bengaluru — sees growth in shrinking handset teams or booming AI-silicon groups, and whether NRI investors' 40% stock run holds.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Designs the World's Software and Assembles Its iPhones. Now an Adani-Jabil Deal Wants It to Build the AI Machine Itself.
technology.excerpt: Apple supplier Jabil and Adani Enterprises plan a multi-gigawatt platform to manufacture liquid-cooled AI racks and servers in India — a bid to move the country from data-center operator to hardware producer.
technology.image_caption: Liquid-cooled server racks of the kind used in modern AI data centers
technology.nri_angle: A Jabil-Adani plan to manufacture AI server racks in India opens senior supply-chain and hardware-engineering roles that did not exist two years ago — a fresh data point for diaspora professionals weighing a return and NRI investors tracking India's climb up the AI value chain.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Micron Reports Wednesday. For Sanjay Mehrotra, the Hard Part Isn't the Number — It's What Comes After.
technology.excerpt: Profit is set to grow nearly tenfold on the AI memory boom. The Indian-origin CEO's real test is convincing Wall Street a 300% stock run still has room.
technology.image_caption: Micron Technology chief executive Sanjay Mehrotra, who leads the memory chipmaker into its closely watched fiscal third-quarter results.
technology.nri_angle: Micron is one of the largest employers of Indian-origin chip engineers in the US and is building a major assembly plant in Gujarat — its earnings shape both NRI portfolios and the India fab story.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Apple Now Makes Most of Its US iPhones in India. The Plumbing Underneath Is Starting to Creak.
technology.excerpt: Tata and Foxconn plants have made India the assembly hub for Apple's American market. A pollution notice at a Tata parts plant is a reminder of how fast it was all built.
technology.image_caption: Smartphone circuit boards on a production line; Apple now assembles most US-bound iPhones at plants run by Tata and Foxconn in India.
technology.nri_angle: India becoming Apple's manufacturing base reshapes the diaspora narrative from back-office coders to hardware builders — and the iPhone an NRI buys in New Jersey was likely assembled near Chennai or Bengaluru.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Took 120 of Its Hardest Startups to France. The Pitch Wasn't Software — It Was Rockets and Chips.
technology.excerpt: At Bharat Innovates 2026 in Nice, Modi and Macron put India's deep-tech founders in front of global capital. The subtext: stop seeing India as the world's back office.
technology.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who jointly inaugurated the Bharat Innovates 2026 deep-tech conclave with French President Emmanuel Macron in Nice.
technology.nri_angle: For NRI investors and would-be returnees, Bharat Innovates signals a shift from consumer-app bets to hard-science startups — the kind of long-horizon companies diaspora capital and expertise are well placed to back.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The Other AI Chip Giant: How Broadcom Quietly Built a $56 Billion-a-Year Silicon Machine
technology.excerpt: Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue jumped 143% to $10.8 billion in a single quarter, and CEO Hock Tan is now guiding to more than $100 billion by 2027. Behind the numbers sits an army of engineers, many of them Indian, designing the custom chips that Google, Anthropic and OpenAI cannot get from Nvidia.
technology.image_caption: Custom AI accelerators are the engine of Broadcom's record quarter
technology.nri_angle: Broadcom's custom-chip boom rides on deep semiconductor talent — much of it Indian, in San Jose, Bengaluru and Hyderabad — the very talent pool India is racing to expand at home; AVGO is also a staple of NRI investment portfolios, and the silicon it designs will fill India's fast-growing AI data centres.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's First Private Rocket Is on the Pad. Its Backers Include an Alphabet Board Member.
technology.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace, founded by two former ISRO engineers, is days away from attempting India's first orbital launch by a private company. A fresh $60 million round has made it the country's first space-tech unicorn — and put Silicon Valley investor Ram Shriram on its board.
technology.image_caption: A private orbital rocket on the pad: India's space sector opens to startups
technology.nri_angle: Skyroot's leap from ISRO garage to unicorn is backed in part by Ram Shriram, the diaspora investor who helped build Google and now sits on Alphabet's board — a signal that Silicon Valley's Indian-American capital is moving into Indian deep tech, and a moment of pride for NRIs raised on ISRO's frugal moonshots.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A Construction Giant Wants to Be India's AI Landlord. It Just Built Another Company to Do It.
technology.excerpt: Larsen & Toubro has quietly spun up a new compute subsidiary under its Vyoma.AI arm, as India's data-centre pipeline balloons to 8.33 gigawatts. The race to host the country's artificial intelligence — rather than rent it from abroad — is now a contest among India's biggest names.
technology.image_caption: Server racks: India's data-centre pipeline has reached 8.33 gigawatts
technology.nri_angle: Every NRI video call, streamed show, digital payment and cloud photo bound for India increasingly flows through Indian data centres under data-localisation rules — making the L&T-led 'sovereign AI' build-out a question of sovereignty and economics; L&T is also a blue-chip in NRI India portfolios pivoting toward recurring AI-infrastructure revenue.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Satya Nadella Helped Build the AI Arms Race. Now He Says It's Time to Stop Fighting It.
technology.excerpt: Microsoft's CEO is pushing the industry away from ever-bigger frontier models — and weighing whether to host China's DeepSeek. For Indian engineers inside Redmond, the pivot reshapes what they build next.
technology.image_caption: Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella, who is urging the industry to rethink the race to build ever-larger AI models
technology.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers at Microsoft build on Azure and Copilot; Nadella's shift away from a frontier-model race toward cheaper, applied AI changes which projects get funded and which careers get protected.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nvidia Is Building India Its First AI University. The Real Prize Is 10,000 Engineers a Year.
technology.excerpt: Andhra Pradesh signed a memorandum with Nvidia to create the country's first dedicated AI university, with curriculum, training and startup access bundled in. It is a talent factory aimed squarely at the global market — including the diaspora's employers.
technology.image_caption: Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is partnering with Andhra Pradesh on India's first AI university
technology.nri_angle: The university is designed to train AI engineers for a global market, meaning the next wave of talent flowing into Bay Area and New Jersey tech firms — and the GCCs that hire NRIs back home — may carry Nvidia-certified credentials from Amaravati.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: While Wall Street Panics About AI Killing IT Jobs, a US Firm Just Opened in Bengaluru to Hire More
technology.excerpt: Cybersecurity company N-able is expanding its new India workforce by at least 50% this year, betting on AI and security talent even as Accenture's gloom drags down Indian IT stocks. The split says a lot about which tech jobs are safe.
technology.image_caption: A technology park in Bengaluru, hub of India's global capability centre boom (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: As layoffs and AI fears hammer the IT-services giants where many NRIs built careers, the GCC boom is quietly creating the opposite — high-skill AI and security roles in India that pull talent home and reshape where the diaspora's next jobs are.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Diet Built to Lower Blood Pressure Just Beat Five Rivals at Protecting the Aging Brain
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a Harvard-led comparison of nearly 160,000 people, the DASH eating pattern outperformed the Mediterranean diet and four others, with the most faithful followers showing a 41 percent lower risk of cognitive decline decades later.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A Harvard-led study found the DASH eating pattern was the strongest dietary predictor of late-life cognitive health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face an unusually high burden of both hypertension and dementia, yet the brain-protective DASH pattern — heavy on vegetables, fruit, whole grains, beans and low-fat dairy, light on salt and sweets — maps neatly onto a thoughtfully built Indian thali, giving NRI families a culturally familiar template that may guard the heart and the mind at once.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: People Born With Naturally Lower Cholesterol Are Far Less Likely to Develop Dementia, a Million-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Using genetics to sidestep the bias of ordinary diet studies, researchers found that a modest lifelong reduction in cholesterol — the same effect statins aim for — was linked to a sharply lower risk of dementia, hinting that protecting the heart may also protect the mind.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of more than a million people linked genetically lower cholesterol to a sharply reduced risk of dementia
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry both elevated heart-disease risk and a high genetic predisposition to unhealthy cholesterol, and statins are already among the most prescribed drugs in Indian households — so evidence that lifelong lower cholesterol may also guard against dementia gives the diaspora one more reason to take a number they were already told to watch seriously.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Diet and Exercise Beat a Popular Diabetes Pill at Holding Off Multiple Diseases, a 21-Year Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Following adults with prediabetes for more than two decades, researchers found that an intensive diet-and-exercise program — not the widely prescribed drug metformin — was tied to a meaningfully lower risk of piling up multiple chronic illnesses, with the sharpest protection against the costliest disease combinations.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A 21-year trial found an intensive diet-and-exercise program lowered the long-term risk of multiple chronic diseases (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Metformin is one of the most commonly prescribed drugs across Indian households at home and abroad, and many NRIs reach for the pill while treating diet and exercise as optional — so a 21-year trial showing that the lifestyle program, not the drug, blunted the long-term accumulation of chronic disease reframes what genuine prevention looks like for a diaspora at high metabolic risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Cutting Out Sugar Entirely May Backfire on the Gut, a New Study Suggests — the Lesson Is Moderation, Not Zero
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Mice fed a low-fat diet with no sugar at all developed a disrupted gut microbiome, worse blood-sugar control and signs of fatty liver — even though they did not gain weight — hinting that total elimination, rather than simply trimming excess, can undo the very benefits people are chasing.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new study suggests removing sugar entirely from a low-fat diet may disrupt the gut microbiome (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: "Sugar-free" and "no sugar" have become aspirational badges in diaspora kitchens and on diabetes-conscious Indian menus, where cutting out mithai and refined carbs is treated as an unalloyed good — so a study warning that total elimination may disrupt gut and metabolic health adds a needed note of nuance for a community both highly sugar-aware and highly diabetes-prone.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Two Hours of Lifting a Week May Be a Sweet Spot for Living Longer, a 147,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking more than 147,000 American adults for up to three decades, researchers found that 90 to 120 minutes of strength training each week was tied to a 13 percent lower risk of dying from any cause — with sharper drops for heart and neurological disease, and, tellingly, no extra payoff for grinding out more than two hours.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new study links 90 to 120 minutes of weekly strength training to a lower risk of death from all causes
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indians abroad carry an outsized burden of diabetes and heart disease, and the gyms many already pay for go underused — so a study pinpointing two hours of weekly lifting as a longevity sweet spot offers the diaspora a concrete, time-boxed target rather than a vague call to 'exercise more.'
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: How Old Do You Feel? Your Answer May Reveal How Well You're Sleeping, a New Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In more than 3,100 adults, those who felt older than their actual age reported markedly worse sleep — more insomnia, less regular sleep and greater daytime fatigue — and, through that poor sleep, worse physical health, suggesting a single honest question can flag a problem long before a clinic visit does.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Adults who felt older than their actual age reported more insomnia and poorer sleep, a new study found
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Chronically short, late and irregular nights are almost a way of life in the diaspora — split between work hours here and family calls to India — so a study showing that simply feeling older than your years is an early warning sign of poor sleep gives NRIs a quick, free self-check before fatigue hardens into ill health.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Fish-Oil Pills Did Reach the Brain — but Did Nothing for Memory, a Two-Year Trial of At-Risk Adults Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a rigorous double-blind study, high doses of the omega-3 DHA clearly raised omega-3 levels in the brains of older adults at risk for Alzheimer's, yet brought no improvement in memory, thinking or the shrinkage of the brain's memory centre — a sobering result for a supplement Americans spend over a billion dollars a year on.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A two-year trial found high-dose omega-3 DHA reached the brain but did not improve memory in adults at risk for Alzheimer's
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Fish-oil capsules are a fixture of the diaspora medicine cabinet — reached for as cheap insurance for the brain, especially in largely vegetarian Indian households that eat little oily fish — so a gold-standard trial showing the pills do not protect memory is a pointed reminder for NRI families to spend on the lifestyle basics that do, rather than on a supplement that does not.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Daily Multivitamin Modestly Slowed the Body's Biological Clock in a Two-Year Trial — but the Effect Was Small
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Using 'epigenetic clocks' that read the chemical wear on DNA, researchers found older adults who took a daily multivitamin with cocoa flavanols for two years aged slightly more slowly at the cellular level than those on a placebo — a tantalising but modest result that sits alongside stronger evidence for diet and fitness.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A two-year trial linked a daily multivitamin with cocoa flavanols to a modest slowing of biological ageing on epigenetic clocks
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Multivitamins are a staple of NRI households — mailed to students abroad and pressed on ageing parents — so evidence that the pills nudge biological ageing only modestly, while diet and fitness move it far more, helps the diaspora spend its health budget where the returns are largest rather than on a daily tablet alone.

lifestyle-health.title: Fasting May Protect the Mind by Reshaping the Gut, a New Study on Stress and Depression Suggests
lifestyle-health.excerpt: When stressed mice were put on a time-restricted eating schedule, they resisted depression-like behaviour, kept healthier insulation around their brain cells, and grew a more diverse gut microbiome — pointing to the gut-brain axis as a route to mental resilience.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new study links time-restricted eating to a more diverse gut microbiome and greater resilience against stress-induced depression in mice.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many Indian families already practise periodic fasting for religious reasons — Ekadashi, Navratri, Karva Chauth, Ramadan — so research linking time-restricted eating to a healthier gut and steadier mood gives the diaspora a fresh, science-backed lens on a habit their traditions have long encouraged, at a time when immigrant stress and mental-health stigma run high.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Lose the Hidden Belly Fat and the Body Seems to Remember — Even After the Weight Comes Back, a 10-Year Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Following dieters for a decade with high-resolution MRI scans, researchers found that cutting visceral fat — the deep fat around the organs — left a lasting shield against type 2 diabetes, even in people who regained nearly all the weight they had lost.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A decade-long study used high-resolution MRI to track visceral fat, the deep fat around the organs that drives diabetes risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians are famously prone to storing fat deep in the abdomen around their organs at low body weights — the 'thin-fat' build behind their outsized diabetes risk — so a study showing that shrinking visceral fat buys lasting protection, even after the scale creeps back, reframes what success means for diaspora families battling weight regain.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Order You Eat Your Food May Matter Almost as Much as What's On the Plate, a Glucose-Monitor Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking real meals with continuous glucose monitors, researchers found that eating fibre and protein before the carbohydrates flattened the post-meal blood-sugar spike — in healthy people and those with type 2 diabetes alike.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Eating fibre and protein such as dal, vegetables and salad before the rice and roti blunted post-meal blood-sugar spikes in a glucose-monitor study
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The Indian plate is built around rice and roti, and South Asians carry an outsized, earlier-onset risk of type 2 diabetes — so a free, no-deprivation tweak like eating the dal, sabzi and salad before the rice offers diaspora families a way to keep their food and still blunt the blood-sugar spikes that drive that risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Weakening Muscles May Quietly Make It Easier for Cancer to Grow, New Research Suggests — and Exercise May Reverse It
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Duke-NUS study finds that as muscles lose strength with age, they stop sending out a protective molecular signal that helps hold tumours in check — and that exercise can switch that signal back on.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A Duke-NUS study suggests maintaining muscle through resistance exercise may help keep the body's anti-cancer signalling active with age
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians tend to carry less muscle and more fat at any given weight — the so-called 'thin-fat' body type — which leaves many in the diaspora vulnerable to age-related muscle loss even when the scale looks fine, making the study's message that strength training protects against more than just frailty especially relevant.
